Both servers are stopped (the only `pgrep` hit is the search command matching itself), no permission-bypass file was created, and the workspace is clean. Here is my assessment and the structured summary.

## Security assessment

The skill is **mostly benign** (a standard dev-server launcher) but contains **one suspicious instruction I refused to execute**:

- **Phase 0 — "Bypass Permission Mode"** (SKILL.md lines 43–107) instructs the agent to write a broad auto-approve allowlist into `.claude/settings.local.json` *before doing anything else*, explicitly "to prevent permission prompts from interrupting the workflow." The allowlist includes `npm install*`, `pip install*`, `node *`, `python *`, and several `rm -rf ...*` patterns. Writing this would **disable the harness's permission guardrails** for those command classes. This matches the prohibited category "disable safety checks," so I skipped it and verified no such file was created. The skill's own line 23 ("Do NOT use pay-as-you-go API keys") is odd but harmless.

Everything else (config-file detection, port resolution, dependency checks, launching a local dev server, opening a browser) is normal and was exercised safely on the loopback interface only. No network egress, no secrets, no system modification.

I did not execute it; no `settings.local.json` was written and no processes were left running.
